canDo: Turn recurring errors into actionable personal rules and replacement chunks.
review: Sort the Error Book by frequency.
input: Listen: three recordings, « Je viens pour le vélo de l’annonce », « Elle écrit les sous-titres des films » and « Faut-il accepter les chiens au bureau ? », twice each; read: the comparison grid « Faire réparer son téléphone » and the articles « « J’ai tenu un mois sans rien acheter de neuf » » and « L’indice de réparabilité a-t-il changé nos achats ? », questions first, then the text.
output: Rewrite / re-say the 20 most frequent ones.
checkpoint: Each error has a closed loop: “error → rule → correct example → new example”.
challenge: Today’s challenge: sort out your Error Book: rank the top 5 errors by frequency, turn each into an actionable “personal rule” (e.g. « Après si, jamais de conditionnel ») with a French chunk you can reuse as is; then do 5 matching exercises for each at Le Point du FLE to check whether the rule really helps you avoid the error.

questions.why: « Allez, mille euros. Marché conclu » — The haggling: asked 1100 → offered 950 → 1050 with extras → settled at 1000 including lock and panniers.
« c’est le français qu’il faut maîtriser à la perfection » — Je choisis: her answer to the charge of betrayal — she keeps the meaning, the tone and the emotion.
« ne peut pas se faire aux dépens des autres » — aux dépens de = at the expense of; the conditional ferait baisser marks a finding still to be confirmed.

V48-01.exZh: Cap your error notebook at twenty entries at most.

V48-02.exZh: You mean I should talk about my current job?

V48-03.exZh: Actually, what I mean is that price isn’t the only criterion.

V48-04.exZh: Rephrasing costs no points; answering beside the point costs a lot.

V48-05.exZh: When people speak fast, “il est allé” sounds like “il était”.

V48-06.exZh: If the conversation has moved on, avoid going back.

V48-07.exZh: Correcting too late draws attention to the mistake.

V48-08.exZh: Examiners think very highly of this sentence.

V48-09.exZh: You can do it, but watch out for tiredness.

V48-10.exZh: My neighbour asks me three questions, any three.

V48-11.exZh: He doesn’t speak very well, but it doesn’t matter at all.

V48-12.exZh: Before the exam, it’s useful to know where you really stand.

V48-13.exZh: You answer three sentences without searching? Then it’s mastered.

V48-14.exZh: These instruction verbs look alike, but they don’t ask for the same thing.

V48-15.exZh: These errors come from connected speech rather than vocabulary.

V48-16.exZh: Checking the route removes a real source of worry.

V48-17.exZh: Listen to short clips on a loop.

V48-18.exZh: Don’t do a full mock exam the day before the test.

V48-19.exZh: Several details can still lose you marks.

V48-20.exZh: I did a mock exam last Saturday.

V48-21.exZh: Arrive early, but stay away from the group discussing everything.

V48-22.exZh: Seen that way, two properly corrected essays are worth more than five.

V48-23.exZh: I think it essential to reread your notebook before writing.

V48-24.exZh: Your sense of your own level is a very poor indicator.

V48-25.exZh: In your email, start by setting out the facts in order.

V48-26.exZh: I’d like some details about the opening hours.

V48-27.exZh: To sum up, two serious corrections are worth more than five papers.

V48-28.exZh: You have two options: send the document or come and drop it off.

V48-29.exZh: I accept this postponement on one condition: delivery before Friday.

V48-30.exZh: The difference is that the second option is free.

V48-31.exZh: Said something wrong? Correct yourself and carry on.

V48-32.exZh: Nobody will hold it against you.

V48-33.exZh: Many candidates leave the sentence hanging.

V48-34.exZh: Resist the temptation to rewrite the whole sentence.

V48-35.exZh: Write down the wrong sentence exactly as you wrote it.

V48-36.exZh: Playing something down reduces the force of what you’ve just said.

V48-37.exZh: Nuancing means drawing a distinction within your own position.

V48-38.exZh: This paper compares nothing: it argues in favour of option A.

V48-39.exZh: The tiredness it causes far exceeds the information gained.

V48-40.exZh: Lack of sleep makes it harder to find words.

V48-41.exZh: When an instruction contains two verbs, deal with them in order.

V48-42.exZh: Missing the negation reverses the meaning of the sentence.

V48-43.exZh: Real speakers correct themselves: “Tuesday, I mean, Wednesday”.

V48-44.exZh: With five new papers, you’ll mainly build up fatigue.

V48-45.exZh: This week I’m doing nothing new: I’m rereading my cards.

title: Final pass over your mistakes
